I am farming only 5 mu, and I am 75 years old, so I will keep things simple, familiar, and manageable with the labor and money I have. I will stay with the wheat-maize rotation because I know this system well, it fits my land, and I have well irrigation, so I can protect yield in dry periods. For wheat, I will use improved seed rather than anything complicated, give moderate fertilizer, irrigate at the key times, and do rotary tillage because it is easier for me than deep ploughing. For maize, I will also keep to a stable, high-yield hybrid, use a bit more nitrogen than wheat, irrigate when needed, and control pests only a few times because on a small farm I do not want excessive cost or labor. I will not push for the highest possible input level; I will aim for steady production that matches my age, my experience, and my small farm conditions.
